IR.V.A.K1.why: VOR accuracy check required before IFR use, course to be flown along airway centerline or direct course, and required IFR navigation equipment

IR.V.A.K2.why: 91.205(d)(2) requires navigation equipment suitable for the route flown, which is the regulatory hook for GNSS suitability, RAIM and WAAS. Database currency and interference are handled by AC 90-100/90-105 and the AFM supplement, not Part 91

IR.V.A.R1.why: Autoflight and FMS management is technique and ADM. Part 91 imposes no autopilot use requirement on a single-pilot Part 91 operation

IR.V.A.R2.why: Task saturation and disorientation are human factors covered in the IFH and PHAK, not regulation

IR.V.A.R3.why: 91.205(d)(2) requires navigation equipment suitable for the route, which is the only regulatory statement about navigation system capability. The specific limitations come from the AFM supplement

IR.V.A.S1.why: VOR equipment check required within the preceding 30 days for IFR operation, including the check log entry

IR.V.A.S10.why: SRM and CRM are Aviation Instructor's Handbook and PHAK material, not regulated

IR.V.A.S2.why: Position determination is technique, described in the Instrument Flying Handbook

IR.V.A.S3.why: Setting and orienting to a course is technique, not regulated

IR.V.A.S4.why: 91.181 fixes the course that must be flown, which is what an intercept establishes. Intercept angle itself is technique

IR.V.A.S5.why: ACS performance tolerances, not regulatory limits

IR.V.A.S6.why: Requirement to operate along the centerline of the airway or the direct course between navigational aids or fixes

IR.V.A.S7.why: PIC under IFR in controlled airspace must report navigation, approach or communication equipment malfunctions to ATC as soon as practical

IR.V.A.S8.why: MFD interpretation is equipment technique, not regulated

IR.V.A.S9.why: Autopilot use is not regulated for Part 91 single-pilot operations

IR.V.B.K1.why: DPs and STARs are complied with as ATC clearances under 91.123. 91.177 sets the minimum IFR altitudes the procedure altitudes must respect. Climb gradient design criteria are in TERPS, which this corpus excludes

IR.V.B.K2.why: PIC final authority, compliance with ATC clearances and instructions, and required IFR position and status reports

IR.V.B.R1.why: Compliance with clearances and instructions, and the IFR communication requirements

IR.V.B.R2.why: 91.221 is the only Part 91 rule on traffic alert and collision avoidance equipment and its use. TIS and ADS-B In traffic display limitations are AIM material

IR.V.B.R3.why: 91.113(b) vigilance to see and avoid other aircraft, which applies in VMC regardless of flight plan

IR.V.B.S1.why: Required communication and navigation equipment for IFR, plus the VOR check before IFR use

IR.V.B.S10.why: SRM and CRM are handbook material, not regulated

IR.V.B.S2.why: Checklist discipline is technique. Part 91 mandates checklist use only for large and turbine-powered aircraft under subpart F

IR.V.B.S3.why: Preflight action requires the PIC to become familiar with all available information concerning the flight, which is the hook for current charts and publications

IR.V.B.S4.why: Timely compliance with ATC instructions and the required two-way IFR communications

IR.V.B.S5.why: Course to be flown, and compliance with the route in the clearance

IR.V.B.S6.why: Charted procedures are complied with as issued clearances and instructions

IR.V.B.S7.why: ACS performance tolerances, not regulatory limits

IR.V.B.S8.why: In-flight weather interpretation is Aviation Weather Handbook material. 91.103 covers preflight weather only

IR.V.B.S9.why: Datalink weather display use and latency are AIM and AC 00-63 material, not Part 91

IR.VI.A.K1.why: 91.175(a) requires use of a prescribed standard instrument approach procedure, and (c) governs operation below MDA. LP versus LNAV guidance differences are AIM and chart material

IR.VI.A.K2.why: Annunciations and mode behavior are avionics specific, documented in the AFM supplement and AIM, not regulation

IR.VI.A.K3.why: Required IFR navigation equipment and the VOR accuracy check. System operating principles are handbook material

IR.VI.A.K4.why: Stabilized approach and energy management are Instrument Flying Handbook concepts, not regulated for Part 91

IR.VI.A.R1.why: Deviating from the cleared approach is a clearance deviation under 91.123 and a departure from the prescribed procedure required by 91.175(a)

IR.VI.A.R2.why: Selecting and confirming a frequency is technique. 91.171 covers only the periodic VOR accuracy check, not per-approach tuning

IR.VI.A.R3.why: Autoflight management is technique, not regulated

IR.VI.A.R5.why: Stability criteria and descent rate limits are handbook and SOP material, not Part 91

IR.VI.A.R6.why: Deteriorating weather bears on the flight visibility and visual reference requirements in 91.175(c) that permit continuing below MDA

IR.VI.A.R7.why: 91.175(c) prohibits operating below MDA unless the required visual references are distinctly visible and the aircraft is continuously in a position for a normal landing

IR.VI.A.S1.why: 91.175(a) requires the approach be flown as the prescribed standard instrument approach procedure

IR.VI.A.S10.why: Landing minimums and the visibility requirement come from 91.175(c) and (d). Inoperative aircraft equipment is governed by 91.213(d). Inoperative ground component adjustments come from the chart inoperative components table

IR.VI.A.S11.why: MDA is the regulatory floor the descent is flown to under 91.175(c). The stabilized profile itself is technique

IR.VI.A.S12.why: The -0 feet side of the MDA tolerance is the 91.175(c) prohibition on descending below MDA. CDI and airspeed tolerances are ACS only

IR.VI.A.S13.why: 91.175(c) lists the visual references required to continue, and 91.175(e) requires the missed approach when they are not available

IR.VI.A.S14.why: MFD use is technique, not regulated

IR.VI.A.S15.why: SRM and CRM are handbook material

IR.VI.A.S2.why: IFR communications requirements. Phraseology itself is AIM material

IR.VI.A.S3.why: VOR accuracy check before IFR use, and the requirement for navigation equipment suitable for the route and procedure

IR.VI.A.S4.why: Compliance with ATC clearances and instructions

IR.VI.A.S5.why: Malfunction must be reported to ATC under 91.187, and continued operation with inoperative equipment is governed by 91.213

IR.VI.A.S6.why: 91.123(a) requires the pilot to inform ATC when unable to comply with a clearance or instruction

IR.VI.A.S7.why: Checklist use is technique for light aircraft under Part 91 subpart A and B

IR.VI.A.S8.why: Configuration and approach speed are AFM material

IR.VI.A.S9.why: Accurate tracking of radials, courses and bearings is the 91.181 requirement. The numeric tolerances are ACS only

IR.VI.B.K1.why: Prescribed procedure and DA/DH rules in 91.175, and inoperative equipment handling in 91.213(d). Descent rate computation is handbook material

IR.VI.B.K2.why: Display, annunciation and mode behavior are avionics specific, not regulated

IR.VI.B.K3.why: VOR accuracy check and required IFR navigation equipment. Signal integrity and interference are AIM and AC material

IR.VI.B.K4.why: Stabilized approach and energy management are handbook concepts

IR.VI.B.R1.why: Clearance deviation under 91.123 and departure from the prescribed procedure required by 91.175(a)

IR.VI.B.R5.why: Stability criteria are handbook and SOP material

IR.VI.B.R6.why: Deteriorating weather bears on the flight visibility requirement in 91.175(c) for continuing below DA/DH

IR.VI.B.R7.why: 91.175(c) prohibits descent below DA/DH without the listed visual references and the required flight visibility

IR.VI.B.S1.why: 91.175(a) requires the approach be flown as the prescribed standard instrument approach procedure

IR.VI.B.S10.why: DA/DH and visibility requirements under 91.175(c) and (d), and inoperative aircraft equipment under 91.213(d)

IR.VI.B.S11.why: Establishing a descent rate matching the glidepath is technique

IR.VI.B.S12.why: DA/DH is the regulatory decision point under 91.175(c). Deflection and airspeed tolerances are ACS only

IR.VI.B.S13.why: 91.175(e) requires an immediate missed approach when the required visual references are not distinctly visible at DA/DH

IR.VI.B.S14.why: 91.175(c)(1) permits continuing only when the aircraft is continuously in a position from which a descent to landing on the intended runway can be made at a normal rate of descent using normal maneuvers

IR.VI.B.S15.why: 91.175(c)(1) ties the visual segment to a normal descent to the touchdown zone. The stabilized path itself is technique

IR.VI.B.S17.why: SRM and CRM are handbook material

IR.VI.B.S3.why: VOR accuracy check before IFR use and required IFR navigation equipment

IR.VI.B.S4.why: Compliance with ATC clearances and instructions

IR.VI.B.S5.why: Malfunction reporting to ATC and inoperative instrument and equipment rules

IR.VI.B.S6.why: 91.123(a) requires notifying ATC when unable to comply

IR.VI.B.S7.why: Checklist use is technique for light aircraft under Part 91

IR.VI.B.S8.why: Configuration and airspeed are AFM material

IR.VI.B.S9.why: Accurate tracking of radials, courses and bearings is the 91.181 requirement. Numeric tolerances are ACS only

IR.VI.C.K1.why: 91.175(e) prescribes when a missed approach is required and that the published procedure be followed. FMS and autopilot behavior is avionics material

IR.VI.C.R1.why: Deviating from the published missed approach or ATC instruction violates 91.123 and 91.175(a) and (e)

IR.VI.C.R2.why: The decision to hold, divert or reattempt is constrained by the IFR fuel reserve requirement in 91.167. The decision itself is ADM

IR.VI.C.R4.why: An early missed approach is permitted and a go-around below DA/MDA is required by 91.175(c) and (e) when references are lost. The triggering factors are ADM

IR.VI.C.S1.why: 91.175(e) requires prompt execution of the missed approach, and 91.183 requires reporting to ATC

IR.VI.C.S10.why: Any subsequent approach, alternate or holding fix must be requested and complied with as an ATC clearance under 91.123, using the IFR communication requirements of 91.183

IR.VI.C.S2.why: Power and pitch for the go-around are technique and AFM material

IR.VI.C.S3.why: Configuration per manufacturer instructions is AFM material

IR.VI.C.S4.why: Checklist use is technique for light aircraft under Part 91

IR.VI.C.S5.why: 91.175(e) requires flying the published missed approach. An alternate missed approach is an ATC instruction under 91.123

IR.VI.C.S6.why: 91.123(a) requires notifying ATC when unable to comply with a clearance or instruction

IR.VI.C.S7.why: ACS performance tolerances, not regulatory limits

IR.VI.C.S9.why: SRM and CRM are handbook material

IR.VI.D.K1.why: 91.175(a) requires the prescribed procedure and (c) and (e) govern circling minimums and the circling missed approach. Approach category speed ranges are defined in Part 97, which this corpus excludes

IR.VI.D.R1.why: Circling is flown under the prescribed procedure and the 91.175(c) visual reference and MDA requirements

IR.VI.D.R2.why: Night and marginal visibility circling still requires the 91.175(c) flight visibility and continuous visual reference. The added risk is handbook material

IR.VI.D.R3.why: 91.175(e)(2) requires a missed approach whenever an identifiable part of the airport is not distinctly visible while circling

IR.VI.D.R5.why: Circling altitude, speed and radius management is technique and TERPS design, not Part 91

IR.VI.D.R6.why: Low altitude maneuvering, stall, spin and CFIT risk are handbook material. 91.119 minimum safe altitudes expressly does not apply when landing

IR.VI.D.R7.why: 91.175(e)(2) governs the missed approach initiated while circling, including the climbing turn toward the landing runway

IR.VI.D.S1.why: The circling maneuver is flown within the prescribed procedure under 91.175(a) and the MDA and visibility rules in (c). Turbulence and windshear allowance is technique

IR.VI.D.S2.why: ATC restrictions are complied with under 91.123. Traffic pattern direction at a non-towered airport comes from 91.126(b), and 91.127 applies the same rule in Class E surface areas. Flagging the 91.126 addition since it was not in the original Part 91 pointer

IR.VI.D.S3.why: SRM and CRM are handbook material

IR.VI.D.S4.why: MDA and the circling altitude floor come from 91.175(c). Configuration and stabilization are technique

IR.VI.D.S5.why: The -0 feet floor is the 91.175(c) MDA prohibition. The other tolerances are ACS only

IR.VI.D.S6.why: Visual maneuvering to base or downwind is technique

IR.VI.D.S7.why: 91.175(e)(2) prescribes the initial climbing turn toward the landing runway and continuing to the missed approach course

IR.VI.D.S8.why: Touchdown point, maneuvering and bank limits are ACS tolerances and AFM limits, not Part 91

IR.VI.E.K1.why: PIC final authority for the landing decision, and the 91.175(c) conditions that must exist to continue to a landing. Environmental and meteorological factors themselves are handbook material

IR.VI.E.K2.why: The approach light system and the other runway lighting and marking cues are enumerated in 91.175(c)(3) as the required visual references. Sign, marking and lighting design is AIM chapter 2 material

IR.VI.E.K3.why: Landing profiles and configurations are AFM and handbook material

IR.VI.E.R1.why: 91.175(c)(1) requires the aircraft be continuously in a position for a normal rate of descent using normal maneuvers, which is the regulatory expression of a stable approach

IR.VI.E.R2.why: Glidepath adherence for light aircraft is technique. The Part 91 glide slope rule in 91.129(e) applies only to large or turbine-powered airplanes at towered airports

IR.VI.E.R3.why: 91.175(c) defines the visual references and flight visibility required to transition from instrument to visual for landing

IR.VI.E.S1.why: 91.175(c) governs the transition below DA/DH or MDA to visual conditions for a normal landing

IR.VI.E.S2.why: ATC advisories and instructions are complied with under 91.123, and NOTAM review is required by 91.103(a). Wake turbulence and windshear avoidance is AIM material

IR.VI.E.S3.why: Checklist use is technique for light aircraft under Part 91

IR.VI.E.S5.why: SRM and CRM are handbook material

IR.VII.A.K1.why: 91.185 prescribes the route, altitude and leave-clearance-limit rules for two-way radio communications failure, including when to begin the approach. 91.3(b) supports deviation in an emergency

IR.VII.A.R1.why: Causes of radio failure are equipment and technique. Part 91 addresses the response, not the cause

IR.VII.A.R2.why: 91.185 is the prescribed lost communications procedure that a deviation departs from

IR.VII.A.S2.why: Re-establishing communications by alternate frequency, relay or transponder code is AIM material, not Part 91

IR.VII.A.S3.why: 91.185(b) and (c) fix the route and destination decision after communications failure

IR.VII.A.S4.why: 91.185(c)(3) fixes when to leave the clearance limit and begin descent and approach

IR.VII.A.S5.why: SRM and CRM are handbook material

IR.VII.C.K1.why: The approach is still flown as the prescribed standard instrument approach procedure under 91.175. Single-engine approach technique and performance are AFM and Airplane Flying Handbook material

IR.VII.C.R1.why: Engine failure risk during approach is handbook and AFM material

IR.VII.C.R2.why: Element is marked [Archived] in the ACS and has no content to map

IR.VII.C.R4.why: Low altitude maneuvering, stall, spin and CFIT risk are handbook material

IR.VII.C.R5.why: Task saturation and disorientation are human factors, not regulation

IR.VII.C.R6.why: Single-engine go-around risk is AFM and handbook material

IR.VII.C.S1.why: Recognizing the failure and maintaining control is technique

IR.VII.C.S10.why: 91.9(a) prohibits operating outside the operating limitations in the approved flight manual, markings and placards

IR.VII.C.S11.why: Circling minimums and the visual reference requirements are in 91.175(c) and (e). The approach category speed ranges themselves are in Part 97, which this corpus excludes

IR.VII.C.S13.why: Checklist use is technique for light aircraft under Part 91

IR.VII.C.S14.why: SRM and CRM are handbook material

IR.VII.C.S2.why: Engine shutdown and simulated feathering are AFM procedures. 91.109 covers dual controls, safety pilots and ATP flight tests but contains no simulated engine failure provision, so nothing in the list fits

IR.VII.C.S3.why: Control and trim technique per manufacturer recommendation, AFM material

IR.VII.C.S4.why: Manufacturer emergency procedures are AFM material

IR.VII.C.S6.why: The approach clearance must be requested and complied with under 91.123 using the IFR communications of 91.183

IR.VII.C.S7.why: ACS performance tolerances, not regulatory limits

IR.VII.C.S8.why: 91.175(c)(1) requires arrival at MDA or DA/DH in a position from which a normal descent to landing can be made

IR.VII.C.S9.why: Deflection tolerance on final is an ACS standard, not a regulatory limit

IR.VII.D.K1.why: 91.187 requires reporting instrument and navigation malfunctions to ATC under IFR in controlled airspace, and 91.213 governs operating with inoperative equipment

IR.VII.D.K2.why: 91.205(d) enumerates the instruments required for IFR, which defines what a primary instrument loss means. Failure modes themselves are handbook material

IR.VII.D.R1.why: Secondary and standby display use is avionics and technique material

IR.VII.D.R2.why: Partial panel aircraft control is technique from the Instrument Flying Handbook

IR.VII.D.R3.why: Task saturation and disorientation are human factors, not regulation

IR.VII.D.S1.why: 91.123(a) requires notifying ATC when unable to comply, and 91.187 requires reporting the malfunction that caused it

IR.VII.D.S2.why: The partial panel approach is still flown as the prescribed standard instrument approach procedure under 91.175. The partial panel technique is handbook material

IR.VII.D.S3.why: SRM and CRM are handbook material

IR.VIII.A.K1.why: 91.7(b) requires the PIC to discontinue flight when unairworthy, 91.405(a) requires discrepancies be corrected between flights or recorded, 91.405(c) requires inoperative items be placarded, 91.213(d) governs flight with them inoperative, and 91.417 sets the maintenance record requirements

IR.VIII.A.R1.why: PIC responsibility for determining airworthiness, and the owner or operator duty to have discrepancies repaired or recorded

IR.VIII.A.S1.why: Recording and correcting discrepancies under 91.405, the maintenance record requirements of 91.417, and the placarding and deferral rules of 91.213(d)
